properties.note.bank_left_out.one: {n} placed sprite needs another bank in this slot, so the game leaves them out.
properties.note.bank_left_out.other: {n} placed sprites need another bank in this slot, so the game leaves them out.
properties.note.bottom_screen: The player arrives on the bottom screen, and the fade into it crosses screens.
properties.note.camera_bottom_offset: The game moves the camera up or down only as far as keeps the player between two lines down the screen. The lower is 128 pixels down plus this.
properties.note.camera_bottom_offset_spe: The lower line in that second mode.
properties.note.camera_fallback: The camera settings this view uses, which are edited in the Cameras tab. None have ID {id}, so the game uses the level's first ({first}).
properties.note.camera_id: Views name camera settings by the low byte of this ID; one naming an ID none has gets the first. {used}
properties.note.camera_lead: The camera settings this view uses, which are edited in the Cameras tab.
properties.note.camera_none: The camera settings this view uses, which are edited in the Cameras tab. The level has none.
properties.note.camera_scroll_height: 15 is none. Anything else has the game note a camera height this many tiles above where it rests on the view's floor; what reads it has not been traced.
properties.note.camera_shared: Views with the same camera values share one camera settings entry, which is made and removed as they change.
properties.note.camera_top_offset: The game moves the camera up or down only as far as keeps the player between two lines down the screen. The upper is 64 pixels down plus this.
properties.note.camera_top_offset_specia: The upper line in the game's second camera mode, which is used while the player is on a chainlink fence, as in W4 Tower.
properties.note.camera_zoom: In sixteenths: 16 is the normal zoom, and so is 0. The game keeps it between 8 and 24; 255 leaves the zoom as it is.
properties.note.closed_to_player_1: The first player cannot enter this entrance.
properties.note.closed_to_player_2: The second player cannot enter this entrance.
properties.note.connected_pipe: The player rides a path to the other end rather than warping. Target stage is then the path's ID, and Target area is kept for the ride: the game's headers call it travelling the path backwards.
properties.note.entrance_id: The number other entrances and the level header name this one by.
properties.note.entrance_type: How the player arrives, and for doors and pipes how they leave. The game's tables stop at Vine: Nintendo's levels use the connected mini pipes after it, but the game reads past its tables for them.
properties.note.entrance_view_id: The view the player arrives in, which bounds the camera and picks the music. 255 is none.
properties.note.exact_x: The player arrives at the entrance's own X. Without it most types move the player half a tile right, onto the middle of it.
properties.note.exit_only: The player can arrive here but cannot enter it.
properties.note.header_layer_first: The {layer} image's tiles. Its colours and screen are the {layer} entries', in the Layers tab.
properties.note.header_other: The header holds three of each, and the game loads the first. What reads the others has not been traced.
properties.note.header_tileset_first: Its colours are the first tileset entry's palette, in the Layers tab.
properties.note.layer_fallback: No entry has this ID, so the game uses entry {entry}.
properties.note.layer_id: Views name a {block} entry by this ID; one naming an ID no entry has gets the first. {used}
properties.note.layer_lead: The {block} entry this view uses, which is edited in the Layers tab.
properties.note.layer_no_screen: That entry shows no screen, so this view has no {block}.
properties.note.layer_rotates: 0xFF00 here has the views naming this entry turn with the stage, as the rotating rooms of World 8 Final Castle do. No other level in the game uses it.
properties.note.layer_rotates_raw: The field the checkbox above reads. Only 0xFF00 does anything; G04_1 and J07_1 hold their tileset's number here, which the game ignores.
properties.note.layer_screen_image: The {layer} image the views naming this entry show. 65535 shows none.
properties.note.layer_tileset_tiles: It does not change the tiles: every view shows the level's one tileset, the Course tab's.
properties.note.level_layer: The level's {layer} image: its tiles, its colours and its screen.
properties.note.level_tileset: The level's tileset, and its colours.
properties.note.mini_physics: Every player moves as Mini Mario does.
properties.note.palette_first: The colours of the whole level's {block}: the game loads them from the first {block} entry only.
properties.note.palette_other: Unused: the game loads the {block}'s colours from the first entry only.
properties.note.pipe_and_cannon_range: Changes how far from the players pipes and cannons stay in the level.
properties.note.scroll_speed_y: The low nibble is a speed and the next a scroll mode. 65535 hides the layer in the views naming this entry.
properties.note.settings_raw: Every settings bit, the named ones above among them.
properties.note.spawn: Coming in here the player stands at {player_x}, {player_y} and the screen's top left corner is at {x}, {y}.
properties.note.spawn_ds_menu: The toolbar's DS menu draws it.
properties.note.spawn_no_view: No view has this ID, so nothing bounds the camera or scrolls the layers.
properties.note.spawn_zoom: This entrance changes the zoom, which the prediction leaves out.
properties.note.start_as_mini: Every player starts the level as Mini Mario.
properties.note.target_area: 0 stays in this area, and the stage and group are then ignored. Otherwise the area's number plus one.
properties.note.target_entrance: The ID of the entrance the player comes out of.
properties.note.target_event: The event this actor activates when it fires.
properties.note.target_group: 0 is this world, otherwise the world's number plus one.
properties.note.target_stage: 0 is this stage, otherwise the stage's number plus one. On a connected pipe, the ID of the path it follows.
properties.note.trigger_event: The event that has to be active for this actor to act.
properties.note.unknown_0x10: Nothing in the game's entrance code reads this byte.
properties.note.unknown_0x11: Anything but 0 replaces the warp: entering fades out and back in within this area, ignoring the target. What the number means beyond that has not been found.
properties.note.unknown_0x20: Nothing in the game's entrance code reads this bit.
properties.note.unnamed_value: This actor does not name the value {value}, which is what these bits hold.
properties.note.unused_06: Unused, likely left over from a migration of the level format: it mostly holds this layer's graphics set 2 number, in the first entry (as in A01_1) or, in J08_1 only, the second.
properties.note.unused_08: Unused, likely left over from a migration of the level format, next to 0x06's graphics set 2: 65535 in every level.
properties.note.vertical_offset: Moves the image up or down in steps of eight pixels.
properties.note.view_rotates: The view turns with the stage, as the rotating rooms of World 8 Final Castle do. Checking it adds the rotating tileset entry 1 the view names, and unchecking it on the last view to turn removes it.
properties.note.wipe_fade: Entering fades with a wipe from one screen to the other, in place of the character's own shape.
properties.note.world_map_node: 0: a normal entrance. 1 to 254: entering it exits the level to the world map, with the player on map node (this number minus 1). 255: exits to the world map where the player already stood.
properties.note.wrap_around: The level loops sideways onto itself.
properties.warning.mismatch: The first {block} entry has {differing}, not {graphics}. Picking here sets them to match; the advanced mode keeps them apart, here and in the Layers tab.
properties.warning.no_entry: The level has no {block} entry, so it has no {block} colours. Add one in the Layers tab.
properties.warning.no_tileset: The game animates the tileset every frame by this number without checking for none, so it calls whatever lies far past its table, which can crash.
properties.warning.rotator_plain: Tileset entry 1 does not rotate, so this cannot add the rotating one there. The advanced mode edits the entries themselves.
properties.warning.rotator_used: Tileset entry 1, which views {views} use, does not rotate, so this cannot add the rotating one there. The advanced mode edits the entries themselves.
